clue.text: Money earned with time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A plain statement that pay is what you get for putting in the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a worker's regular pay is the money earned for labour.

clue.text: Beastly types used to be on Midlands team

parts.note: were is the past tense of be, so it stands for used to be
Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, a football club in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Fierce characters who once played for a Midlands football club.
explanation.walkthrough: WOLVES is Wolverhampton Wanderers, a football club in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycanthropes of folklore turn into savage animals, so they are literally beastly creatures.

clue.text: Political group, inexperienced, somewhat ignored by Liberal

parts.note: someone green is new and untried

indicators.note: the Liberal is left out, so its letter is dropped from the word for somewhat

parts.note: partly means to some extent, somewhat

explanation.surface: A political group of novices, rather snubbed by the Liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored by Liberal' removes L from PARTLY, leaving PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the environmentalist organisation that fields candidates in elections is a political party.

clue.text: Area between hill and forest, scene of tumult

indicators.note: the area letter is placed between letters of the hill word, splitting it

parts.note: a berg is a mountain or hill, as in South African usage
Arden is the forest of Shakespeare's As You Like It, and a real Warwickshire woodland

explanation.surface: A patch of land lying between a hill and a forest turns out to be a place of uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' sets A inside BERG, giving BEARG.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a pit for bear-baiting, the phrase now means any rowdy, disorderly place.

clue.text: King, aces and queen: enough for the rubber

parts.note: ER is Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher of a King Edward
an ace is A, so two or more aces are AS
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A card player's hand of king, aces and queen is enough to win the rubber at bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubber' looks like a bridge term, but in British English it is the thing that rubs out pencil marks.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a rubber is the small block used to remove pencil marks.

clue.text: Account about Ostrogoth leader in classical language

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the Ostrogoth letter goes inside the classical language

parts.note: Latin is the language of ancient Rome

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the start of Ostrogoth

explanation.surface: A history of the Ostrogoth leader written in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a relation is a narrative or telling of events, an account.

clue.text: Various oven treats including a sort of toast

indicators.note: the anagram takes in the single letter from a
various suggests the letters of oven treats in assorted arrangements

explanation.surface: A selection of baked goodies plus some kind of toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges OVEN TREATS into VOTRESANTE, and 'including' puts A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'to your health', it is a drinking toast.

clue.text: Democrat has trouble in parliament

parts.note: to ail is to be troubled or unwell

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician runs into difficulty in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dáil Éireann is the lower house of the Irish legislature.

clue.text: Fruitcakes, or ingredients for them

definitions.meaning: fruitcakes is slang for crazy people, lunatics
a fruitcake recipe often has almonds or walnuts in it

explanation.surface: Musing on fruitcakes, either eccentric people or the cakes and what goes in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for crazy people, and literally kernels baked into a fruitcake.

clue.text: Some angling equipment about to be removed from fisherman's basket

indicators.note: the letter for about is taken out of the basket word

parts.note: a creel is a wicker basket for carrying caught fish
C is circa, the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: An angler takes some gear out of the fishing basket.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa, about) taken out of CREEL leaves REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the winding device on a fishing rod that holds the line is part of an angler's kit.

clue.text: Street on island in which you'll see bird, one flying high

indicators.note: the street is placed on, i.e. after, the island part
the bird is to be found inside the island's name

parts.note: Bali is an Indonesian island
a loon is a diver, a water bird

explanation.surface: A tourist on an island street spots a bird and someone soaring overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A balloon pilot travels high in the air, so is one flying high.

clue.text: In cold season, daughter gets short inexpensive jacket

indicators.note: the following letters go into the cold season word

parts.note: winter is the cold season

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: cheap means inexpensive

explanation.surface: In winter, a daughter acquires a bargain jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last letter off the word for inexpensive; 'In' sets daughter plus that trimmed word inside the cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: A light outer coat that keeps out the wind is a kind of jacket.

clue.text: English male brought in recent reforms, main focus of attention

indicators.note: the English male is put inside the rearranged word
reforms suggests reshaping the letters of recent

parts.note: a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: Recent reforms have brought an Englishman into a key role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' turns RECENT into CENTRE, and 'brought in' sets ESTAG between its R and final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something occupying the middle of the theatre's acting area is in the spotlight, the main focus.

clue.text: Later chats about what cardinal might be wearing

indicators.note: about signals the letters of later chats moved around

explanation.surface: Gossip afterwards about a cardinal's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinals of the Catholic Church wear red headgear as a sign of their rank.

clue.text: Lady in pants cuddles friend in vivacious fashion

indicators.note: the anagram hugs the friend inside it
pants is British slang for rubbish or poor, so the letters of lady in are jumbled

parts.note: mate is a British word for friend

explanation.surface: A woman wearing trousers hugs her pal in lively style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' rearranges LADY IN into ANIDLY, and 'cuddles' puts MATE inside it. 'pants' looks like trousers; in British slang it also means rubbish, hence the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with lively spirit is doing it vivaciously.

clue.text: Memorised several books on Shakespearian king

indicators.note: the books are placed on, i.e. after, the king

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of a Shakespeare tragedy
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone has committed to memory several volumes about King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having learned something by heart is having memorised it.

clue.text: Frenchman distributed narcotics, losing tons

indicators.note: distributed suggests the letters spread about into a new order
losing means the word gives up a letter

explanation.surface: A French drug dealer peddled narcotics but lost tons of stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tons' removes T from NARCOTICS, and 'distributed' rearranges NARCOICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a French island, so a native of it is a Frenchman.

clue.text: Swimmers in shallow water struggle to move

definitions.meaning: flatfish that live on the sea bed in coastal waters
to thrash about clumsily, unable to make progress

explanation.surface: Bathers in the shallows thrash about trying to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish species found in shallows, and a verb for struggling clumsily.

clue.text: Completely new drain installed in cathedral city

indicators.note: the following pieces are fitted inside the city's name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
to tire is to drain or exhaust

explanation.surface: A brand-new drain has been fitted throughout a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drain' looks like plumbing, but here it is the verb meaning exhaust. ELY is a small English cathedral city near Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wholly or totally.

clue.text: At home, after taking remedy for starters, I am fit

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: for starters takes the first letters of taking and remedy

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone at home, having taken their medicine, declares themselves healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person in good physical condition is said to be fit.

clue.text: Customer contributes little money to a pool of tips, mostly

parts.note: P is a penny, a small amount of British money

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tronc is a shared pool of tips in a restaurant, split among staff

explanation.surface: A diner chips in a few coins to the staff tip pool.
explanation.walkthrough: TRONC, a restaurant's shared tips fund, loses its final C under 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a regular client of a shop or restaurant is a patron.

clue.text: Custom in South America to wolf down chorizo ingredient?

indicators.note: custom goes inside the letters for South America

parts.note: usage is custom or habitual practice
to wolf food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A tradition in South America of gobbling up spicy sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: AM is a standard abbreviation for America. The question mark flags the definition as by example: chorizo is a sausage, so its filling counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorizo is a sausage, so minced filling for sausages would go into it.

clue.text: Fancy wife getting together with that man

parts.note: him is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A man fancies his wife getting together with another fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sudden fancy or caprice.

clue.text: Small amount of pollution corporation's reversed

indicators.note: reversed means the word for corporation's is read backwards

parts.note: corporation is jocular British slang for a pot belly, a tum, so corporation's is tum's

explanation.surface: A company's minor pollution incident gets undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company; jocular British slang uses it for a big belly, TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A speck of soot or dirt is a small particle of pollution.

clue.text: Out of danger, with demon and hydra overthrown

indicators.note: overthrown suggests demon and hydra toppled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hero is safe after defeating a demon and a hydra.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: safe and having succeeded, with no risk left.

clue.text: Publicity for church in part of Africa

indicators.note: for here means standing after, so the publicity follows the church

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, publicity

explanation.surface: Advertising on behalf of a church in an African region.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a landlocked country in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Old French statesman having little time during US college trip

indicators.note: the time letter sits inside the college letters

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
T is the abbreviation for time
an errand is a short trip to do a task

explanation.surface: A former French politician squeezes in a short visit to an American university.
explanation.definitionFit: François Mitterrand was President of France from 1981 to 1995.

clue.text: Guy is into pasta — yummy!

indicators.note: is into says the answer is found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A man is a big fan of pasta and finds it delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man; it is a rope that braces a tent or mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a supporting rope or wire on a mast or tent is a stay.
